podcast.title: Lenient First Album Contract
podcast.body: Her family initially hesitated to allow an 11-year-old Björk to record an album, but they proceeded after one small Icelandic record label offered a "permissive" and "relaxed," rather unprofessional, contract. "uno de los contratos de una de las pequeñas escograficas era bastante permisivo y bastante relajado, poco profesional."

podcast.title: Major Icelandic Artist
podcast.body: Björk is highlighted as a prominent Icelandic artist, representing the country's unique musical output. "el grandísimo caso de Bjork que yo creo que es la isla Andesa."

podcast.body: Marcus Draves, producer of Mumford & Sons' debut album, had previously produced an album for Bjork before early 2009. "one by Bjork."

podcast.title: Mark Bell Collaboration
podcast.body: Starting with the *Homogenic* album, Björk began a significant and lasting collaboration with Mark Bell, who would work with her for nearly the remainder of her career. This partnership was instrumental in her shift towards harder and more experimental electronic sounds, moving away from trip hop. "ella empieza a trabajar con Mark Bell, persona con la que acabaría trabajando casi el resto de su carrera."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Mentorship and Record Label
podcast.body: Björk has been supportive of other female artists who express themselves in different ways, mentoring them through the record industry and signing some to her own record label. "And she's been very kind to other female artists who have different ways of expressing themselves, mentoring them through the record industry and signing some of them to her own record label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Mother's Album Artwork
podcast.body: Björk's mother, Gipee, designed and created all the artwork for her 1977 debut album, contributing to its homemade feel. "su madre Gipee fue la que hizo la portada hizo todo el rasgortístico del álbum."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Move to London and Experimentation
podcast.body: Feeling that Iceland was too small for her ambitions, Björk relocated to London, where she commenced extensive experimentation with music, sounds, and visuals, a creative process she continues to this day. "Iceland was way too small for Bjork so she moved to London where she began to experiment with music and sounds and visuals, something that continues to this day."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nellee Hooper Collaboration
podcast.body: Björk's collaboration with Bristol-based producer Nellee Hooper was a pivotal moment in her musical evolution, introducing her to the rhythmic foundations of trip hop and electronic music. Hooper, known for his work with Massive Attack, Tricky, and Portishead, was a key figure in shaping the sound of the 90s, guiding Björk into a more electronic sound. "Bjork conoce a Nilly Hopper, importante productor musical de Bristol, que había sido amigo de Massive Attack, de Tricky, de la gente de Portishead y que fue una persona clave para entender parte del sonido de los 90, ayuda a introducirse a Bjork a lo que serían las bases rítmicas del trip Hop y de la electrónica."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Non-Musical Activism and Art Collaborations
podcast.body: Beyond music, Björk is widely known for her dedication to environmental defense, animal rights, and ecology. She also frequently engages in collaborations with various art forms, including video creations with non-musical artists. "Sus proyectos no musicales por los que VR que es más conocida es un poco por el trabajo que hace por la defensa de media ambiente, por la recencia de los animales, por la ecología, por todas estas cosas, pero también un poco por todas las colaboraciones que hace con las de la variedía de arte, con proyectos de videocreaciones y de artistas que no son exactamente musicales."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Performance at Tibetan Freedom Show
podcast.body: Bjork performed at the inaugural Tibetan Freedom Show held at Golden Gate Park in San Francisco on July 15, 1996, which was a major event for raising awareness and funds for the Milarepa Fund. "The line up included the Beastie Boys, plus the smashing pumpkins, Bjork, Sonic Youth, the Chili Peppers, and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Performances with Nature Motifs
podcast.body: Around the time of *Utopia*'s development, Björk's appearances often featured her surrounded by natural plants and dressed in bird or nature-inspired costumes, leading to speculation about a potential nature-themed album. "Hacia esas actuaciones rodeadas de plantas naturales y disfrazadas de pájaro y de naturaleza."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Lo que rodea a Björk y Utopia

podcast.title: Pioneer of Audiovisual Formats
podcast.body: Björk was recognized as the first artist to release a single on DVD, establishing her as a significant precursor in the adoption of audiovisual formats. Her deep engagement with visual work is evident in her videoclips, which are often considered works of art. "ella fue la primera artista en publicar un single en DVD y siempre ha sido una de las grandes precursoras de los formatos audiovisuales."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Pioneering Audiovisual Artist
podcast.body: Björk is recognized as a visionary artist, consistently ahead of her time in audiovisual projects. She now almost exclusively works on fully audiovisual projects, blending her music with creative visual elements, evidenced by her numerous DVDs, and she largely presents her projects in museums. "Siempre es una de las grandes adelantadas a su época en este tipo de proyectos, ya prácticamente solo trabajen proyectos completamente de obisuales, en los que combina su música con proyectos creativos audiovisuales, bueno, todos sus DVDs, pero es que ya prácticamente ya solo trabajen museos haciendo sus proyectos."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Pop Culture Icon
podcast.body: Following the release of her 1993 album *Debut*, Björk ascended to the status of a pop culture darling, maintaining this influence throughout the remainder of the decade and beyond. "Bjork became a pop cultured darling for the rest of the decade and beyond and let me tell you something."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Remix Pioneer
podcast.body: Björk developed a very early vision for remixes, understanding them as authentic reinterpretations of her composed material. She not only encouraged other artists to remix her tracks but also created her own, even re-recording entire parts of songs for these remix versions, a practice that foreshadowed their later popularity. "Bjork desarrolla una visión muy temprana de lo que vienen a hacer las reméclas que serían tan populares y que son hoy en día y ya no solo las reméclas. Ella regraba, se reace partes enteras de las canciones para hacer solo en las reméclas."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Retrospective Art Exhibit
podcast.body: In 2015, Björk was the subject of a retrospective art exhibit at the New York Museum of Modern Art, a rare honor for an artist of any medium. "Bjork is one of the few artists to be the subject of a retrospective art exhibit, which is exactly what happened at the New York Museum of Modern Art in 2015."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Rolling Stone Top Singers Ranking
podcast.body: Björk is ranked number 60 on *Rolling Stone* magazine's list of great voices and singers. "este depuesto número 60 en la lista de las grandes voces y cantantes que hizo la revista Rolling Stone."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Sampled by Burial
podcast.body: Burial has sampled Björk's vocals in his own work, reinterpreting her singing in his characteristic processed style. "esta es villosa cantando y este es burial coge en la villa se veis esto es increíble o sea este es ásier cantando en concierto este es ásier pues reinterpretado por burial."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Sampled in Endtroducing.....
podcast.body: Björk is mentioned as an artist whose song fragments are credited in DJ Shadow's album *Endtroducing.....*. This indicates that while many samples came from obscure, uncredited sources, some recognizable artists' work was intentionally incorporated and acknowledged. "hasta Vior, que está creído en el Entrodius, porque hay fragmentos de alguna canción de Vior."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Shrinking but Loyal Fanbase
podcast.body: Despite creating an album of immense quality like *Utopia*, Björk's audience is characterized as increasingly loyal but also progressively smaller. This situation suggests that while her dedicated fans cherish her work, her sound is becoming more alienating to a broader public, leading to reduced sales and chart performance. "El público de Bjork a la vez que cada vez más fieles cada vez más reducido."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Slug Genitals Vinyl
podcast.body: Björk released a single on vinyl that she herself described as "slug genitals color," a detail humorously noted as being printed on the vinyl's sticker. "os juro por Dios que la mismísima Bjork lo ha dicho y así lo he escrito en la pegatina del vinilo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Support for Independent Movements
podcast.body: While generally not overtly political, Björk has supported various independent movements, including those in Tibet, Kosovo, and Greenland. "And while she's not overly political, she tends to shy away from that, she has also been supportive of various independent movements, including Tibet, Kosovo, and Greenland."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Synth Pop's Continued Presence in the 90s
podcast.body: While 80s-style Technopop declined in the 1990s, elements of synth pop continued to live on and be present in her music. "It did, however, live in some respects in the music of nine-inch nails, de Pesh mode, radio head, and Bjork."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Roots of New Wave through Techno-Pop

podcast.title: The Sugar Cubes' Antics
podcast.body: While a member of The Sugar Cubes, the band once gained unauthorized entry to a local government radio station and broadcast what they considered "proper music" until they were arrested. "The Sugar Cubes and they by the way once broke into a local government radio station and played what they thought was proper music until they were arrested."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Sugar Cubes' Success
podcast.body: Formed in 1986, The Sugar Cubes were embraced by the Gen X rock community for their "right brand of weirdness" until their breakup in 1992, with Björk serving as the central figure of their appeal. "The Sugar Cubes were the right brand of weirdness for the Gen X rock community and they were embraced from the time they were formed in 1986 until they break up in 1992."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Transition to Museum Artist (Medúlla onwards)
podcast.body: From the *Medúlla* album onwards, Björk's career evolved significantly, marking her transition from primarily being a singer to becoming a "museum artist" or a "videocreator." This phase emphasizes her deepening engagement with visual arts and her work being presented in art institutions. "empieza posiblemente la parte de Bjork ya no tanto como una cantante sino como directamente una artista de museo o una videocreadora."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Ubiquitous 90s Electronica Artist
podcast.body: Anything Björk did in the 1990s was broadly considered Electronica, showcasing her significant presence and versatility within the genre's wide-ranging definition. "And just about anything Bjork did in the 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unconventional Artistic Identity
podcast.body: Björk is renowned for her highly unconventional artistic approach; virtually nothing she produces is considered "normal," a characteristic that endeared her to alt-rock enthusiasts in the 1990s and established a recognizable "Bjorkish" style. "Nothing Bjork does and I mean nothing. She does is what anyone would call normal and that's exactly what made her such a darling to the alt rock kids in the 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unique Artistic Approach
podcast.body: Over four decades, Björk has consistently stood out as a singer, songwriter, producer, and actor. Her approach is so distinctive that her name has become an adjective ("Bjorkish") to describe something experimental, unique, and "left of center." "If I say that something is Bjorkish, you'll immediately understand that I'm talking about something so left of center that it describes most descriptions."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Unique Artistic Identity ("Björk-ish")
podcast.body: Björk is recognized for such an eclectic, experimental, and forward-looking approach to music that the term "Björk-ish" is widely understood to describe her unique style, which transcends even her notable fashion choices like the swan dress. She is from Iceland, where her distinctiveness is considered "rather normal." "if you describe anything as Bjorkish, everyone knows exactly what you mean, and that goes beyond wearing a dress that looks like a swan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unique Vocal Style
podcast.body: Björk possesses a distinctively massive singing voice, characterized by a "pixie-ish" quality, frequently punctuated by shrieks, howls, growls, and sudden transitions to "little girl whispering." "This pixie-ish thing with a massive singing voice that was often punctuated by shrieks and howls and growls and then back down to little girl whispering."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: VH1 Top 10 Best Female Artists Ranking
podcast.body: Björk is listed at number 29 on VH1's famous list of the 10 best female artists in history. "Bjork está de número 29 en una famosa lista que hizo VH1 de las 10 mejores artisas femininas de la historia."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Vague Album Launch Information
podcast.body: The launch of *Utopia* was uncharacteristically discreet, with Björk providing minimal details throughout the creative process and leading up to the release. This contrasted sharply with her usual practice of offering extensive information about her projects. Album details were confirmed only days before its market debut in November, causing it to be absent from promotional release lists until late. "El lanzamiento de su último disco era como muy distinto, lo hacía sin casi sin datos, Bjork siempre había sido una persona que daba como bastantes datos puntual y durante todo el proceso creativo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Lo que rodea a Björk y Utopia

podcast.title: Venture Capital Fund (Björk)
podcast.body: During Iceland's banking crisis in the late 2000s, she initiated a venture capital fund named "Björk" to support the establishment of sustainable industries in Iceland. "Out of that came a venture capital fund called Bjork that supported the establishment of sustainable industries in Iceland."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Videoclips as Art
podcast.body: Björk's videoclips are celebrated as genuine works of art, with many having been exhibited in museums. Her artistic vision is so compelling that she is one of the few artists to have collaborated with three of the most renowned directors in the field: Spike Jonze, Chris Cunningham, and Michel Gondry. "prácticamente todos los videoclips de Bjork son auténticas obras de arte que a veces han llegado a estar expuestas en museos."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Vocal Contributions to Death Grips
podcast.body: Björk recorded numerous vocal tracks and singing parts specifically for Death Grips, which the band subsequently incorporated into one of their albums. "Bjork grabaría un montón de sus voces y varias partes de ella cantando que luego harían en su siguiente trabajo los Dead Gryps."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Voice Perfection and New Recording Method (Vespertine)
podcast.body: During the *Vespertine* era, Björk underwent extensive singing lessons to perfect her voice, resulting in a less aggressive, more harmonic, and peaceful vocal delivery. Concurrently, she developed a new, more solitary recording system, working primarily alone at home with a computer, moving away from complex studio setups to focus on her individual artistic process. "Bjork recibe muchas clases de canto para perfeccionar su voz y tenemos una manera de cantar de Bjork que cada vez es menos agresiva e intensa y es mucho más armónica y mucho más pacífica ahora, así decirlo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Volta Tour Exhaustion
podcast.body: Following the success of her *Volta* album, Björk embarked on an "incredible and exhausting" two-year tour. This demanding period left her completely drained, leading to a substantial break from music and touring activities for several years. "hizo esa increíble y agotadora gira de dos años que la dejó completamente agotada y después de la cual tendrían enorme pausa."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Volta Tour Psychological Impact
podcast.body: Björk herself described the *Volta* tour as her longest and most psychologically taxing experience, leaving her feeling deeply drained. This intense experience was a primary reason for her subsequent need for an artistic pause. "la esquina más larga y psicologinamente algo tan que tuvo en toda su cara, que la dejó para estar en tu cara psicologicamente y un poco le necesitaba tener una pausa de lo que había sido el éxito del Volta."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Björk y su curioso proyecto con los Dirty Proyectors

podcast.title: World Music Influences in Post
podcast.body: In her *Post* album, Björk significantly broadened her musical palette beyond electronic and indie influences. She began incorporating complex sounds, including Caribbean rhythms, African rhythmic bases, and even elements from Asia, which helped to richly define her evolving sound with global influences. "aquí vienen influencias de ritmos calibeños, de bases rítmicas africanas, incluso de algunas partes de Asia, empiecen incorporar muchos sonidos del mundo que empiezan a requerar mucho ese sonido de Bjork."

xref.body: In 1986, while celebrating Reykjavik, Iceland's 200th anniversary, Bjork and the Sugarcubes broke into a government-run radio station. They proceeded to play songs they considered "realistic," leading to their arrest. "When the city of Rechivec Iceland, celebrating the 200th anniversary of its founding in 1986, Bjork and the rest of the sugar cubes, which was her band at the time, broke into the government-run radio station and played songs they thought were realistic. They got arrested for that."

xref.title: Embrace by Gen X Alt-Rockers
xref.body: Björk's 1993 solo album, "Debut," was released during the height of the Grunge explosion. Her innovative sound and experimental nature resonated deeply with the alt-rock nation of Gen Xers, who were open to new ideas and embraced her, leading her to introduce them to diverse musical styles. "many of the alt-rock nation of Gen Xers were very open to new ideas, they embraced Bjork and she, in turn, taught them something about different musical styles from tripop to cell stuff that was more Yorkish."

xref.body: Despite being considered highly unique and "weird" globally, Björk is regarded as rather normal in her native Iceland, potentially attributed to factors such as the country's cold climate, volcanic gases, or vodka.
